speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill will also amend legislation pertaining to other Home Team Departments (HTDs) where a similar change is being proposed for the CD Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These amendments will allow the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to standardise certain policies across the different HTDs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In this speech, I will be using the term "SCDF officers" to refer to SCDF regulars, National Servicemen (NSmen) and volunteers of all ranks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the first objective of enhancing operational response and efficiency, let me start with the proposals related to SCDF's Public Warning System (PWS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The PWS is a network of outdoor sirens located on rooftops throughout Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The sirens provide warning of threats, such as aerial bombardments, natural disasters, terror attacks and other home-front emergencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They alert members of the public to take actions to keep themselves and their loved ones safe.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many public warning sirens are located on Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks or other Government-owned buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some have to be installed on privately-owned buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, SCDF gets permission from building owners before the sirens are installed on their premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Unfortunately, there have been occasions where permission is not granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some owners cite concerns about noise pollution, even though the sirens are typically sounded for only about six minutes in total in any year, and only during the day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others tell us bluntly that they are not obliged to cooperate, since there is no law that requires them to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result of their refusal to cooperate, SCDF has to look for alternative locations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But this may lead to sub-optimal placement of the sirens, which may result in members of the public in some areas not being able to hear the sirens as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More sirens may even have to be installed to ensure sufficient reach, at increased costs to the public.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We cannot allow public safety to be compromised.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: New section 103C inserted by clause 20 will also provide SCDF with the power to enter premises to conduct assessment, maintenance and repair work for the devices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: New section 103D provides that any willful removal, destruction, damage or tampering of the devices will be an offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An offender is liable for a fine of up to $50,000 and an imprisonment term of up to three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These penalties are aligned to those for similar offences involving telecommunications equipment under the Telecommunications Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF plans to enhance the PWS in the coming years, by installing new types of public warning devices, such as equipment that broadcasts emergency alerts within buildings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: New section 103B read with the new definition of "prescribed civil defence emergency device" also allows SCDF to require building owners to allow SCDF to install devices for the monitoring or detection of a civil defence emergency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The types of devices will be set out in the regulations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The PWS is a long-term initiative, and we hope that building owners recognise the importance of PWS and come on board willingly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Legal action will be taken only as a last resort, against building owners who refuse to cooperate for no good reason.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Next, I will speak about SCDF's ambulance services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are formally known as Emergency Medical Services (EMS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF was unable to confirm the identities of about 8%, or 14,000, of them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Typically, these patients were unconscious or unresponsive and did not carry identification documents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If such patients could have been identified, the ambulance crew would have been able to expeditiously obtain the relevant health information from the Ministry of Health (MOH) and deliver more appropriate and timely medical interventions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For instance, crew members can avoid administering drugs to which the patient has known allergies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Or, if they know that a patient with breathing difficulties has a history of asthma, they can administer the relevant drug immediately.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can also share the patient’s identity with the hospital, so that preparations can already be made at the Emergency Department even while the patient is being conveyed there by SCDF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MHA will work with MOH to grant the authorised personnel access to the relevant health information, strictly on a need-to-know basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To safeguard the information, SCDF will put in place robust information technology (IT) security systems and processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the devices to capture the fingerprints will be password-protected, and the information encrypted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clear guidelines will also be developed to determine the access rights of the personnel involved and the circumstances under which the information can be accessed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All access to the database will be logged, and penalties will be imposed for any misuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF officers often perform emergency and rescue operations which require swift and decisive action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To reach and extricate persons in emergency situations, SCDF officers may have to enter private premises and remove obstacles that block their way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, SCDF officers often have to break down doors and window grills in their rescue operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To allow operations to proceed efficiently and safely, SCDF officers may have to close roads near the incident site, as well as shut gas, water or electricity supplies to affected premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For some types of operation, SCDF officers have been relying on the common law to justify the use of requisite powers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is the case for EMS and rescue operations, as well as operations involving hazardous materials, or HazMat for short.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF officers will be allowed to exercise such powers for the purpose of protecting lives and preventing injury and harm to human health.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In time-critical and dangerous situations, SCDF officers are also often required to take calculated risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, in a rescue operation arising from a road accident, SCDF officers may need to cut open vehicles, to extricate trapped victims.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This risks damage to the vehicles, and even injury to the people inside.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At present, SCDF officers do not have statutory protection from legal liability when they take calculated risks during EMS, rescue and HazMat operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF officers ought to be allowed to focus on the job at hand, on saving lives, without being distracted by concerns about whether they may be charged or sued for damages caused while performing their duties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The protection applies only where SCDF officers act within the scope of the CD Act, and only when they have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So far, I have been speaking only about SCDF officers and what is needed to allow them to do their jobs more effectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But SCDF officers are not the only people performing civil defence operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, SCDF engages ambulances run by Private Ambulance Operators (PAOs) to augment its "995" fleet.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SCDF also has an arrangement with the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) for the training of SAF medics, under which SAF medics are attached to SCDF ambulances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will now move on to the third objective, which is to strengthen SCDF's disciplinary and other HR-related processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will begin with the voluntary extension of service for SCDF NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under the Enlistment Act, the maximum service age for SCDF NSmen is 40 years for those holding the rank of Senior Warrant Officer and below, and 50 for those holding the rank of Second Lieutenant and above.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will allow SCDF to continue tapping their valuable expertise, honed through many years of experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is in line with what SAF and Police NSmen are currently allowed to do.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With this amendment, motivated individuals, such as Mr Jorge Lau, will be able to extend their NS with SCDF on a voluntary basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He was a Deputy Division Commander, holding the rank of Colonel (NS) when he reached the age of 50 last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Lau has had a unique NS experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He underwent his Basic Military Training with SAF before becoming a Police NS Inspector, and later served the rest of his Operationally Ready NS in SCDF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He has held several key appointments in SCDF, including Company Commander, Head of Operations, and Battalion Commander, of a Rescue Battalion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The wealth of operational experience he has acquired over many years of NS puts him in a good position to mentor young SCDF NS commanders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the Voluntary Extension of Service Scheme, SCDF will offer him the opportunity to continue serving.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These volunteers will have the same powers, protection, recognition and benefits as operationally-ready NSmen, and will be subject to the same disciplinary regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Certain provisions of the Enlistment Act will also apply to these SCDF volunteer ex-NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among other things, the volunteers are protected from the loss of civilian remuneration and unfair dismissal, and employers are required to grant these volunteers leave of absence during the period of service.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Next, I will cover the new service offence for SCDF and Police Officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the course of their work, these officers may be exposed to health hazards, such as toxic substances and pathogens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the need arises, SCDF and the Police must have strong levers to compel their officers to go for medical examinations and treatments, including vaccinations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The objective is to protect the health of our officers and prevent the spread of diseases.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 30 amends the Police Force Act to create similar provisions for Police Officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Similar provisions for SAF personnel already exist in the SAF Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the rest of this section, I will speak about the key amendments to SCDF's summary trial process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They involve changes to how service offences are detected, tried and sanctioned within SCDF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The first amendment concerns the time bar for summary trials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At present, an SCDF NSman cannot be subject to a summary trial, if the offence was committed more than three years ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This change will align SCDF’s practice with that of the Police.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second amendment pertains to the recall of NSmen for summary trials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, SCDF issues recall orders under section 14 of the Enlistment Act, to compel its NSmen to answer disciplinary charges levelled against them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such recall orders enable NSmen to claim for the loss of their civilian remuneration under the Enlistment Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With this change, SCDF will not have to make up for the loss of civilian remuneration by affected NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who do not show up for their summary trial will be deemed to have committed another service offence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such provisions for SAF NSmen already exist in the SAF Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The third amendment concerns appeals against outcomes of summary trials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At present, SCDF NSmen below the rank of Lieutenant-Colonel who have committed service offences are tried by SCDF Disciplinary Officers (DOs), while those with the rank of Lieutenant-Colonel or above are tried by a Disciplinary Board.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are currently no avenues of appeal against the decision of the DO or the Disciplinary Board.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The conduct and procedures of an appeal will be set out in regulations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Commissioner SCDF will be the appellate authority.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He will determine the outcome of an appeal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In section 81 as amended by clause 16, Commissioner SCDF will also be given the authority to review any findings and award of punishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The last amendment in this section concerns the maximum fine quanta for disciplinary offences committed by SCDF NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clauses 13 and 14 align the maximum fine quanta for disciplinary offences committed by SCDF NSmen with those for SAF NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clauses 27 and 28 do the same, for disciplinary offences committed by Police NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the powers and protection conferred on SCDF officers, there is a need to deter abuse by impersonators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 22 will make it an offence for any person to impersonate or misrepresent himself as an SCDF officer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, any person who manufactures or sells SCDF uniforms or insignia without authorisation from SCDF will be liable for a fine of up to $10,000 and an imprisonment term of up to three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clauses 26 and 31 create similar criminal provisions in the Immigration Act and the Prisons Act, for acts relating to immigration officers and prison officers respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) of Singapore and the Singapore Prison Service are the other uniformed HTDs that currently do not have such provisions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill plays an important role in enhancing the support SCDF and other HTDs need in their dedicated service to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Similar possibilities exist through the NS volunteer scheme and the Voluntary Extension of Service for Police NSmen Scheme, in the SAF and Singapore Police Force (SPF).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will help advance SCDF's 2025 Vision of building a "Nation of Lifesavers".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Being prepared to save lives would allow for prompter responses to life-threatening incidents and a more robust and resilient response in the event of a national crisis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister elaborate on the rationale of the vision and the initiatives that SCDF has undertaken towards partnering the community to collectively work towards that vision?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second major feature of this Bill is supporting day-to-day operations of the officers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Historically, these duties were performed separately by SCDF and the Singapore Fire Service.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, in 1989, they merged to form Singapore Joint Civil Defence Forces and soon after became known as SCDF.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The SCDF's twin objectives of fighting fires and saving lives can be seen in the Fire Medical Vehicle commissioned in 2017.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This vehicle is a hybrid between the Red Rhino and an ambulance, supporting both objectives of firefighting and saving lives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In recognition that life-saving work is important and a core part of what SCDF does, this Bill provides a statutory basis for the powers that need to be exercised in day-to-day operations – to save lives, for example, by breaking open a door.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There are two additional powers provided by the Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clause 20, in particular, prevents the acts of an individual from compromising the safety of many through refusing to cooperate in the installation or maintenance of the device or even tampering with it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because having a functional and effective PWS is critical for a strong, robust emergency response.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In Palu, Indonesia, the earthquake destroyed the mobile phone network infrastructure, which made it impossible to use that mode of communication to disseminate information.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Having a warning system in place can make the difference between the life and death of many, but only if it is understood, only if vigilance is exercised in detecting the situation and sounding the alert.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As such, would the Minister elaborate on how our systems have been updated and upgraded to detect emergencies, possibly taking in newer warning signs?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister also elaborate how the community is engaged in emergency detection and preparedness?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As the Minister alluded to in her speech earlier, this is a useful and pragmatic improvement as it would allow for a prompter and more accurate diagnosis as medical history may reveal important information, such as possible complications and known allergies.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In this way, the value of a person’s life necessitates that the practical impossibility of obtaining consent from an unconscious person will not bar more targeted help from being rendered to save the person’s life.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: SCDF officers will thus be able to render medical assistance more effectively and efficiently.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The third feature of the Bill is that it prevents impersonation and unauthorised use of the insignias of the SCDF, Immigration and Prisons officers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This prohibition supports the officers’ work by ensuring that the trust that the public has in the Services is not misused by an impersonator.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Immigration Officers keep our borders safe; Prison Officers follow through in implementing incarceration sentences and, where necessary, rehabilitation; SCDF Officers command evacuations, douse fires and save lives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Impersonators should not be allowed to dilute their cause or effectiveness or the trust instilled in our officers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Well done, to our SCDF and Home Team officers!

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Having been instilled with a duty to save lives, SCDF NSmen will be able to formally and regularly advance the mission of saving lives through better powers and a more robust legal framework for the environment within which they operate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This can only be a positive move and I stand in support of it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I seek a few clarifications regarding this Bill which the Minister essentially addressed in her opening speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For a better understanding, could the Minister provide further examples of other day-to-day emergencies which do not constitute as a civil defence emergency?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under clause 3, powers will be given to SCDF officers to enable them to act in good faith and with reasonable care to save lives and prevent injuries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would be helpful to receive clarifications on these circumstances since the powers of SCDF officers are extensive, including breaking into private places and vehicles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could the Minister provide more information on this scheme?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, how would their roles differ from the Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU) or SCDF's volunteer force set up in 2006?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would the ex-NSmen volunteer under a separate scheme?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill also states that the Minister may, from time to time, authorise that the NSmen be paid for their services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I was going to ask about the rationale for this change, but the Minister has answered it in her speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I want to add that the PWS is important as it warns all of us of imminent threats that could endanger lives and properties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know this is not part of this Bill, but what is also equally important is the fire alarm system and we need to address the lack of central fire alarm systems at our HDB blocks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I appreciate that SCDF will be introducing a new requirement for all new residential units, and residential units undergoing works which impact fire safety, to install Home Fire Alarm Devices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is good to provide early warning to the occupants of the affected unit, but what is also important is to provide warning for other residents living in that block.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will not only help all residents in the affected block but also the SCDF officers responding to fight the fire.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Every second counts in a fire emergency and lives will be saved if people are aware of the fire early and can evacuate early.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The dangers our SCDF officers face will also be reduced if people are evacuated early.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We also need to remember that it is not only the fire that kills but, more often than not, also the smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While the fire might be contained in the unit, the smoke is not.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have raised this issue several times already and I sincerely hope that MHA will consider mandating central fire alarm systems at our HDB blocks, similar to what is already present in condominiums.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The proposed measures to provide SCDF officers with clearer legal powers will aid the officers in their day-to-day operations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I do have some questions regarding some of the proposed measures.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I welcome the move to provide SCDF officers and providers of emergency ambulance services with explicit legislative powers for their day-to-day operations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During an incident, where time is of the utmost importance, the last thing that we can afford is for those attending to medical emergencies to hesitate, or have their hands shackled by the uncertainty of the lawfulness of their actions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will allow them to quickly obtain the necessary health information in order to administer the appropriate medical treatment, onsite or otherwise.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would officers have a mobile device that can access such sensitive information remotely, and how can we safeguard these personal data?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I agree with the intention of this measure, I would like to ask if there had been any past cases of impersonation of SCDF officers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If so, what were the intentions of the impersonator to do so?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry be open to consider authorising some vendors, such as those operating in the Beach Road army market, for example, to sell SCDF uniforms to officers who can prove their identity on site?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under the Bill, it is an offence for Home Team officers to refuse to undergo medical examinations and treatments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I can understand the need for this measure to avoid situations where officers refuse to go for such medical examinations or treatments, despite the possibility of exposure to health hazards, I am puzzled as to why refusing dental treatments would be classified as an offence.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps, the Minister could elaborate on what are the examples of dental issues arising from exposure to health hazards, and if there have been any past cases that have compelled the Ministry to designate such non-compliance as an offence.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The CDAU was established in 2006 and the current pool of volunteers consists mainly of ex-NSmen.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: SCDF plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety of Singaporeans and residents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This comes with great sacrifice for SCDF officers, who put themselves at risk constantly and they deserve our nation’s appreciation and gratitude.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One only needs to recall the Pulau Busing fire which happened in March this year.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The massive fire required the deployment of more than a hundred personnel.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Thanks to the hard work of our SCDF officers, the fire did not spread to two nearby oil tanks, which would have made the situation far worse.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What was particularly etched in the minds of many appreciative Singaporeans was the photograph published in many news portals of our fatigued firefighters, many of them NSmen, drenched in perspiration because of the extreme heat, taking rests in between their duties.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These are necessary to allow the SCDF to take necessary and timely actions in day-to-day operations, in particular, to prevent the escalation of an emergency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is a recognition of the dangerous situations that SCDF officers face even in peacetime.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Whilst liability against individual SCDF officers in such circumstances is excluded, may I ask whether it is meant to exclude institutional liability of SCDF?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There may be cases of institutional negligence leading to death.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For example, in a 2000 English case, a pregnant woman had suffered a serious asthma attack at home, and the visiting general practitioner made an emergency call for an ambulance, which took 40 minutes to arrive.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The woman suffered a miscarriage and brain damage.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The ambulance service was found negligent for its unreasonable delay in arriving to the victim’s aid.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Such cases, by and large, are the exception rather than the norm as, under common law, there must be clear evidence of professional negligence by the emergency services crew who need to perform sometimes in exacting conditions.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the English case, the Court focused on the fact that whilst the ambulance service accepted the call to respond, it failed to explain why it had taken 34 minutes to travel 10 kilometres (km), barely 18 km per hour, and why the ambulance log book had been deliberately falsified to show a travel time of about nine minutes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It must also be borne in mind that, in Singapore, hospitals and doctors are not immune to claims against them in respect of the medical care they provide.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I understand the rationale for protecting SCDF officers from personal liability, so long as they act in good faith and act reasonably.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If so, may I please ask what is the rationale for this?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Act presently allows SCDF to direct any person to render assistance to save life in immediate damage, during a state of emergency.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Apart from this, I wonder whether we should give the power to SCDF to instruct members of the public to provide cooperation to handle emergency situations even in peacetime.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Under common law, there is no general duty to come to the rescue of another and, therefore, generally, a person cannot be held liable for doing nothing while another person is in peril.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In contrast, if a person decides to come to the rescue of another, the good Samaritan is said to have assumed a duty of care and can become liable if his action makes the situation worse, such as injuries caused by a reckless rescue attempt.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I filed a Parliamentary Question last month on whether notices to guide the public on the use of automated external defibrillators (AEDs) could be installed in public locations to guide members of the public who have not received training on the use of AEDs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How do we protect such people who step in to help in good faith?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: By providing protection to them, we may encourage more people to use AEDs, fire extinguishers, and go some way to achieve the vision of a nation of life savers that the hon Member Mr Christopher de Souza mentioned in his speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But I would welcome clarifications on the three points I raised from the hon Minister.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a reasonable expectation but somewhat vague.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the event of a tragedy, how do we determine what constitutes "good faith" and "reasonable care"?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is there a list of guidelines or best practices?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In an emergency where chaos reigns, officers may have to make split-second judgement calls under very tremendous stress and heavy constraints.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is there a neutral panel or body which all parties can turn to for additional information, guidance and mediation?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I request for elucidation as I think that more clarity is necessary for all parties concerned to get on the same page, and to empower our officers to carry out their duties with greater confidence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have raised salient issues, which I will now address.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked whether the PWS will be upgraded to incorporate detection capabilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF will provide more information at a later stage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Next, I will address the questions on SCDF's access to the personal information of EMS patients which Mr Melvin Yong asked about, specifically, how the information will be accessed and how it will be protected – all very valid questions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF is keenly aware of the need to safeguard patients' information and has designed several steps to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There will be standard operating procedures (SOPs) to specify the officers who can access the information, as well as the circumstances under which they are authorised to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The information that the officers can access is restricted to what is necessary to provide timely and effective care to the patient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, robust measures will be implemented to reduce the risk of unauthorised access.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, a robust logging and audit regime will be put in place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Access to ICA and MOH's databases will be logged and regularly audited.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Any person found to have abused his access to the information will be severely dealt with.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Persons who commit offences under the relevant legislation, such as the Computer Misuse Act, will be charged in Court.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will now proceed to address questions on the powers and protection for SCDF officers and authorised individuals performing civil defence operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Joan Pereira sought clarification on the circumstances under which the powers and protection will apply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such operations include not only EMS but also rescues.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On a day-to-day basis, SCDF conducts a broad range of rescue operations in response to industrial and traffic accidents, HazMat incidents and also suicide attempts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In all these operations, SCDF officers sometimes have to enter private premises without permission, remove objects that impede operations, evacuate endangered persons, close roads and shut off utilities supplies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will apply only when the officers concerned have acted in good faith and with reasonable care.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: An officer will be judged to have acted in good faith, if his actions were coherent and consistent with the intent to save lives, prevent harm to health, or protect property.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is a very tight condition set around the idea of acting in good faith.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He will be judged to have acted with reasonable care, if his actions were of a standard commensurate with his skill and experience for that particular situation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, again, there is an expectation that the actions must relate to his skill and also his experience in those particular circumstances.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Fire Safety Act has a similar protection for SCDF officers when they perform firefighting operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF will equip its officers with the competence to make the necessary decisions during operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF will continue to put its officers through rigorous training and constantly refine its SOPs to guide their actions during operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That said, we are also cognisant that no training or SOP can cover the full range of operational contingencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, any evaluation of whether an officer has acted in good faith or reasonable care will also take into account whether his decisions were reasonable under those circumstances, for instance, he may be working with incomplete information and dealing with severe time constraints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked whether the proposed protection will apply to SCDF as an institution.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government remains liable for wrongful torts committed by SCDF officers if the SCDF officer did not act in good faith or with reasonable care.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the English case that the Member has cited, it appears that the English ambulance service had been negligent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the event of negligence, the protection from liability will not apply to both the officers concerned and to SCDF, as the condition of "acting in good faith and with reasonable care" would not be met.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF is funded by public monies and has a responsibility to safeguard them from frivolous claims, which the protection will help to prevent.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Next, I will address questions on the proposal to make it a service offence for SCDF and Police Officers not to comply with orders to go for a medical examination or treatment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong was puzzled as to why the relevant provisions cover dental treatments, and I would like to clarify that these dental treatments will only pertain to those required by SCDF and SPF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will ensure that the provision is comprehensive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Currently, we do not have any required dental examination or treatment, but we cannot rule out the possibility of such requirements in the future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is nothing untoward happening now regarding teeth, but we still have to take care, and these will be in support of operational readiness.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A similar provision, Sir, just in case you are curious, requiring dental examinations and treatment can already be found in the existing SAF Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, SCDF is not doing something very unusual.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will move to the unauthorised production, distribution and use of uniforms and insignia.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, in 2014, SCDF received feedback concerning four scammers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong expressed concerns about the impact of the amendments on retailers who are currently selling SCDF, ICA and Prisons uniforms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He asked whether it is possible to allow the retailers to continue selling the items, albeit only to bona fide Home Team officers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When SCDF informed retailers of plans to prohibit the sale and distribution of the items some months ago, the retailers told SCDF that they did not have large inventories of SCDF, ICA and Prisons items, as the sales volumes for such items were low.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is because most SCDF regulars and NSmen prefer to purchase their items from SCDF's own e-mart.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Christopher de Souza cited SCDF's vision of building a "Nation of Life Savers" by 2025 and asked how SCDF intends to realise that vision.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Timely action will allow an incident to be managed before it becomes more serious.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The SCDF has a high standard of emergency response.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it will still take around eight to 11 minutes for fire engines or ambulances to reach any location.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In comparison, a family member or member of the public in the immediate vicinity can provide more immediate assistance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, in 2015, SCDF launched the Save-A-Life initiative to encourage community first-response to cardiac arrests in the HDB heartlands.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF also launched the myResponder app, which alerts first-responders of cardiac arrests in the vicinity and where AEDs are located.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SCDF is now exploring the extension of the Save-A-Life initiative to private condominiums.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In April 2018, the myResponder app was also enhanced, to alert first-responders of minor fires in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This has allowed the first-responders to help SCDF put out rubbish chute fires or provide photos and videos of the fires to SCDF for better sense-making.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During a state of emergency or state of civil defence emergency, SCDF officers have the power to direct any member of the public to render assistance to save lives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked whether SCDF officers should be allowed to exercise such a power for day-to-day civil defence operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The refusal to comply with an SCDF officer's direction is a criminal offence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: An offender is liable for imprisonment of up to three months and a fine of up to $2,000.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The power is necessary during a state of emergency.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In such a situation, Government resources are likely to be stretched.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Under such extraordinary circumstances, SCDF must have the levers to mobilise any civilian resources available, including members of the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is not the case for day-to-day civil defence operations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For SCDF's vision of a "Nation of Life Savers" to be feasible and sustainable, we want members of the public to come forward willingly as community first-responders, and not because they are obliged to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question then is whether enacting a Good Samaritan Law will assuage potential concerns that individuals may have about rendering assistance to others, unintentionally causing harm and being liable for criminal prosecution or civil claims, as Mr Murali Pillai has noted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for criminal liability, this generally requires malign intent which will not apply to a Good Samaritan who acts in good faith.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, we will study this issue further to see if specific legislation is warranted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether SCDF has enough volunteers in CDAU, and whether first-generation PRs can be allowed to join CDAU.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CDAU caters to individuals who are keen to serve as SCDF volunteers in functions, such as firefighting, EMS and public education.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The number of CDAU volunteers has grown from 18 in 2006 to 300 currently.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At present, we have 10 volunteers who are first-generation PRs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We certainly welcome more people to sign up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the difference between the roles of volunteer ex-NSmen and of CDAU volunteers, and the circumstances under which volunteer ex-NSmen will be paid.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, volunteer ex-NSmen serve in NS units, mainly in specialised roles, such as Rescue Battalions and Civil Defence Shelter Battalions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CDAU volunteers, who may not necessarily have served NS with SCDF, perform a broader range of roles such as firefighting, EMS and public education.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, there is a difference in the manner in which they are called to serve.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the case of a volunteer ex-NSman, he can be called up for up to 40 days per work year, mostly for in-camp training.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In terms of scheduling their volunteer duties, CDAU volunteers are given the flexibility to work around their career and family commitments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They typically serve at least 16 hours of duty per month, so it is quite different.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Similar to NSmen, volunteer ex-NSmen receive service and make-up pay when they are called up for duty.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They may also receive additional allowances as key appointment holders.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Typically, residents are familiar with the emergency escape routes for their buildings, which are moreover designed to enable effective smoke dissipation in the event of a fire.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Residential units are also designed to be fire compartmentalised to reduce the risk of fire-spread.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, SCDF will monitor the situation and make adjustments if necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will conclude by addressing a technical amendment that Mr Murali Pillai asked about.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is the amendment to section 115(2), which allows the Minister to make regulations on any matter that may be prescribed under the Act.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Examples include the definition of "prescribed civil defence emergency device" in section 2 or "relevant premises" in the new section 103A.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will enable SCDF to be more effective in saving lives and protecting property.
